release.notes:
**Tears of the Kingdom: the crashes after 20 to 75 minutes, and amiibo.** A tester's TOTK ended five times on v1.010.002 to v1.010.004, each the same way: after 20 to 75 minutes of normal play the game suddenly wrote gigabytes of memory it had never used, until the console's memory ran out (the app closed) or the game stopped by itself ("jumped to an unmapped address"). All five ran with **Settings > Performance > Memory** at 8 GiB and no mods. Not confirmed on a console yet: play TOTK as you did, and send `/data/prosperoeden/logs` if it still ends.

### Fixes

- **Tears of the Kingdom without mods plays with 4 GiB, whatever Memory says.** The larger memory is for mods that need it. A game told it has 8 GiB is handed 6.4 GiB, twice what a Switch gives it, and TOTK fills it: in the four sessions where the memory ran out, the same piece of the game's own code was writing 0.4 to 1.8 GB of new memory within seconds (on v1.010.004, 1.8 GB of free memory was gone within 5 seconds), and in the fifth the game wrote 3.4 GB and then stopped. With 4 GiB it has the memory it was made for. With one of its mods switched on, the memory you chose stands, since the mod may need it; the `Memory layout:` line in `stderr.log` says when this applies.
- **The game's own memory has 1 GiB that nothing else can take.** Nightshade kept 1 GiB of the console's memory free for the game's sudden needs, but only on paper: the graphics, the emulator's own memory and the driver could still take it, or leave it in pieces too small for the game (the crashes found pieces of 1 or 2 MiB). Nightshade now holds that 1 GiB itself, fills it up again ten times a second, and the graphics start giving memory back as soon as the game has used half of it, before the game has to wait. `stderr.log` shows what it holds (`reserve=` in the `EDEN_MEMORY` and `EDEN_CRAM` lines).
- **The system reads the game's data from the right place in long sessions.** When a game hands the system a buffer (a sound to play, a request, a file to save), the emulator reads it where it lies if it is in one piece, and decided that by a number each piece of mapped memory gets. The numbers run out after 65,536 of them, 43 minutes into TOTK, and from then on part of a buffer could be read from the wrong memory. Every page of the buffer is now checked.

release.notes:
## Media Player Classic PS5 1.5.1

A fix for 1.5, which didn't open on the console ([#3](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/MediaPlayerClassicPS5/issues/3); thanks to [Sulfurico-One64](https://github.com/Sulfurico-One64) for the report).

### Fixed

- **1.5 closed at launch with "signal: 12 (SIGSYS)".**
  - **Cause:** to find the folder ShadowMount+ runs the app from, 1.5 used two system functions (`statfs`, `getfsstat`) that only the system's own processes may use. Their library (`libkernel_sys`) stopped the app as it started.
  - **Fix:** the app now uses exactly the same system functions as 1.4. The helper payload, which may use those functions, finds the folder for it.
  - **With an older helper, or none:** the app reads ShadowMount+'s link to the folder instead. It only writes there if that folder is really this app's.
  - **Prevention:** the build now fails if the app ever imports a function outside that set again.
- Everything else is as in 1.5: the new Keys actions, the touchpad pointer, movable windows, and updates into the folder ShadowMount+ runs.

### Installing

- **On 1.4:** Help > Check for updates offers 1.5.1. That update is still installed by 1.4's updater, which writes `/data/homebrew/PPSA99015`. If ShadowMount+ runs your copy from another folder, send the 1.5.1 payload once instead.
- **On 1.5 (the app doesn't open):** send `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.5.1.elf` to your payload loader (port 9021). It writes over 1.5 in the folder ShadowMount+ runs. Then close the app if it is open and start it again from the home screen.
- **To go back to an older version:** a payload never writes over a newer version, so move or delete the app's folder first, then send the older payload. The README's "If the app doesn't open" section has the steps, including the ShadowMount+ steps Sulfurico-One64 found.

### Files

- `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.5.1.elf`: send it to your payload loader (port 9021). It installs the app, then stays as the helper that unlocks it.
- `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.5.1-PPSA99015.zip`: the app folder, used by Help > Check for updates. You don't need to download it yourself.
- `mpc-ps5-v1.5.1-src.zip`: the source.

### Status

Its imports are now identical to 1.4's, which opens on the console, and it passes 470 host tests. **It opens on a PS5** (tested by the author before release). If it doesn't on yours, please tell us in #3, with Options > Miscellaneous > Debug logs on (the log is `/data/mpcps5/logs/boot.log`).

Port by [MisterTemaki](https://github.com/MisterTemaki).

apps.name: Mediathek
apps.summary: Movie library that finds films in a movies folder on internal or USB storage, fetches posters from TMDB and plays them.
apps.author: M0S4YSH3LL0

release.notes:
## Mediathek 0.3.0 (`01.000.030`)

A Netflix-style movie library and player for the PS5. Put your films in a `movies` folder on the internal drive, a USB stick or extended storage; Mediathek finds them, shows a billboard and shelves with their posters, fetches covers and descriptions from TMDB, and plays them. English and German.

### What's new in 0.3.0

- **A richer details page.** It now shows the film's **length**, **video format** (codec, resolution, container), **sound format**, TMDB's **user score** (out of 10) and its **genres** (next to the collection above the title).
- **Languages.** An **Audio** row lists the audio languages of the tracks the app can actually decode, and a **Subtitles** row shows the language of the `.srt` file beside the film, read from its file name (`Film (2011).de.srt`, `Film.English.srt`). A track that does not play is not offered. Untagged tracks show "Unknown language".
- **Read from the file, once.** Length, formats and audio languages are read with FFmpeg when the page opens (headers only, no decoding) and cached, so reopening is instant. "Refresh cover and info" reads the file again.
- **Fewer TMDB requests.** Covers, wallpapers and descriptions are fetched only for films that have no cover; a rescan or restart no longer asks about films that already have one. Films that were fetched before get their score and genres once.

### Features

- **Home:** a billboard for the focused film, tinted by its colours, then shelves: Continue Watching, Recently Added, collections, decades and All Movies.
- **Movies:** an eight-column grid, sortable by title, newest or year.
- **Player:** scrubber, seeking, pause, audio-track and `.srt` subtitle switching, a stream info panel. It remembers where you stopped; 92% counts as watched.
- **Automatic covers:** with a free TMDB key, posters, wallpapers and descriptions are fetched for films that lack them. Pictures you put beside a film always win.
- **Names are read for you:** `Blue Harbor (2011).mkv` and `blue.harbor.2011.2160p.BluRay.x265-GRP.mkv` both work.

### Good to know

- Needs a PS5 that runs homebrew, with a loader that starts apps from `/data/homebrew` and an ELF loader on `127.0.0.1:9021`. Without it the app starts but finds no films.
- Checked on the author's console: start-up, the scan, cover and description download, the details page with its length, formats, score, genres and languages, and a large 1080p H.264 MKV playing with sound.
- **Not yet checked on a console:** the console language detection, 4K and HEVC playback (software decoding, not expected to be smooth), subtitle and audio-track switching, menu sound and rumble, and drives other than the author's.
- Only one `.srt` per film is used. Embedded subtitle tracks are not shown.

release.notes:
## wiliwili PS5 v1.6.0.1

Native Homebrew title application for PlayStation 5 (Title ID: `PPSA99099`).
This release brings compatibility fixes for DLNA casting, resolves critical crashes during search input and application exit, and enhances the home screen presentation with native 4K backgrounds and a full-bleed icon.

---

### 🚀 Key Improvements & Fixes

#### 1. 📡 DLNA Casting Compatibility on PS5
- **Sandbox Network & Port Adaptation**: Adapted to PS5 sandbox network policies with reworked port probing and binding logic, resolving socket option errors and ensuring reliable casting service startup.
- **Upgraded DLNA Core (Renderer & Mongoose)**: Updated the underlying streaming server to properly handle restricted socket options on the console. You can now cast videos directly from the mobile Bilibili app to your PS5.

#### 2. ⌨️ TV-Style Search Experience & Input Crash Fixes
- **TV Virtual Keyboard by Default**: Search now defaults to the TV-friendly virtual keyboard optimized for gamepad controls on fresh installs, eliminating the need to toggle it manually in settings.
- **UTF-8 Character Stream & Crash Fix**: Fixed a fatal exception in wide-character conversion during on-screen keyboard input that could hang the title; resolved multibyte character backspace truncation for smoother, crash-free typing.

#### 3. 🛡️ Lifecycle & Clean Application Exit

release.notes:
## PSP5 01.000.100

PSP5 now follows the console's language, reads games and texture packs from USB drives, and lets you remap the PSP's buttons.

### Interface language

Choose a language under **Settings → System → Language** and the home screen follows it, not just the emulator. 45 languages are available, including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao. The font atlases were rebuilt to carry them, growing from 113 glyphs to 3,055 per face. Right-to-left languages are laid out right-to-left.

Where PPSSPP already translates a term, PSP5 uses its translation. The remainder — favourites, the A–Z view, the cheat panel, the save-state slots, the button names and the description under every settings row — are PSP5's own, shipped as 78 strings in 44 languages under `assets/lang/psp5/`.

**These 78 strings are machine-translated and unreviewed in most languages.** Corrections are a one-line edit in `assets/lang/psp5/<id>.ini`: the files are plain `English = translation`, and a missing line falls back to English.

### Games and texture packs on USB drives

PSP5 now reads drives using the same layout as its own memory stick:

```
/mnt/usb0/PSP/GAME/<your game>.iso        # also .cso, .chd, EBOOT.PBP
/mnt/usb0/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/         # a texture pack, with its textures.ini
```

All eight USB ports (`/mnt/usb0` … `/mnt/usb7`) and both extended drives (`/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`) are scanned. A texture pack on a drive takes precedence over one on the memory stick.

**This requires folder listing to be unlocked.** A PS5 app can open a file by its full path but cannot list a folder, and finding games requires listing. PSP5 requests the unlock at every start, and any of these will grant it: **etaHEN** (enable *Legacy CMD server* in its toolbox), **OnionHEN**, **LegacyJB**, or the **PS5SX2 Helper** (add PSP5 to its `/data/whitelist.txt`).

Without it, PSP5 runs from its own memory stick as before and USB drives appear empty. The reason is recorded in `psp5.log` as `unlock: nothing answered`.

### Button remapping

**Settings → Controls → Buttons** lists all twelve PSP buttons — the four face buttons, both shoulders, Start, Select and the four D-pad directions — with the console button each is mapped to.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Cross** | set the button |
| **Square** | set a second button |
| **Triangle** | clear the second |
| **Circle** | back |

Each PSP button can be mapped to **two** console buttons, so Select can sit on both the touch pad and L3, or L on both L1 and L2.

  answer can no longer freeze a game, and each request is written to the game's log with its
  result and time.
- Games' own non-blocking sockets now really do not wait on the PS5.
- **Router ports:** the PS5 does not let programs use ports below 1024, so a game's port 1000 is
  opened as 11000 on the console. The automatic router request (UPnP) now asks for the game's
  port towards the real one (1000 to 11000). Many routers refuse ports below 1024 that way
  (`UPnP error code 501` in the log); then add the forwarding rules by hand on the router, UDP, to
  your PS5's address: 1000 to 11000, 1001 to 11001, 1013 to 11013 (MW2's; the log's
  `XSocket::Bind` lines show each game's).

Checked on a PS5: Halo 3 online (sessions, connection checks, leaderboards) and MW2 searching
and finding other players' Xbox LIVE matches. Not confirmed yet: joining and playing a whole match
with other people. Please send the game's log from `PPSA50011/logs` with your results.

Since v0.6.0 the phone camera's certificate folder, `PPSA50011/phone-camera`, was made readable

apps.summary: Original Xbox emulator: a port of xemu to the PS5, in alpha.
apps.author: ZiZc3

release.notes:
## XPSemu Update 2.1

**Up to 4 players**
- Every signed-in PS5 user's controller (or a guest's) now works in games. Before, only the first controller was seen.
- Players 2-4 are plugged in within 2 seconds of signing in, even during a game, and unplugged when they sign out.
- Only player 1 controls XPSemu's menus; the other controllers are for the games.

**Game language** (#10)
- New setting: Settings > Interface > Game language (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese).
- Games that include that language now start in it. Before, every game started in English.

**Saves**
- Saves are no longer lost when you leave a game. XPSemu now lets the Xbox finish writing before it stops the game.
- Broken saves are repaired automatically. A save cut off while it was being made could stop a game from saving at all. 
- A backup of every change is kept in `/data/xemu/save-repair/`.
- While the game finishes saving, the Now Playing bar burns away, and you can keep using the menu.

**Fixes**
- Crash after 15-20 minutes in playing games like Ninja Gaiden Black (#7).
- Crash when a game makes lots of new shaders.
- The Xbox hard disk survives a crash or closing XPSemu from the PS5 home screen. Before, games could hang on loading until `xbox_hdd.qcow2` was deleted.
- Far fewer graphics pipelines built, so fewer hitches in effect-heavy scenes.
- No needless ~8 MB cache save every time you leave a game.

**Requirements**

- [kstuff](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite) +`helper.elf`
- [ShadowMountPlus](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)
- Your own Xbox MCPX boot ROM, BIOS and XISO games (not included)

**Installation**

1. Download `PPSA97358.zip`, extract it, and copy `PPSA97358/` to `/data/homebrew/.`
2. Load `helper.elf` with kstuff.
3. Put `mcpx_1.0.bin`and your BIOS`Complex_4627.bin`in`/data/xemu/`.
4. Put your games in `/data/xemu/games/`or in`xemu/games/`on a USB drive.
5. Launch XPSemu from the home screen.

**Note:** to use your own hard disk (for example with the original Xbox dashboard), put it at`/data/xemu/xbox_hdd.qcow2` before starting XPSemu.

apps.name: PShare
apps.summary: Sends the media gallery's captures to Discord, Telegram, a USB drive or a shared folder on your PC.
apps.author: StonedModder

release.notes:
PShare sends your PS5 captures where you want them, the moment you take them. Take a screenshot or save a clip with the Create button and PShare sends it to Discord, Telegram, catbox.moe, a USB drive, a shared folder on your PC or a dozen other places, automatically and in the background, even after you close the app. It doubles as a media gallery: browse every capture by game, watch clips with sound, and open anything on your phone from a QR code

### Features

- Automatic uploads. A small background uploader, pshared, notices each new screenshot and clip, waits until a clip has finished writing, and sends it. It keeps running after PShare closes.
- Many destinations. Discord webhooks, Telegram bots, catbox.moe, Litterbox, any multipart HTTP endpoint, a USB drive or console folder, and PC shares over SMB 2/3. Account-free hosts (Uguu, tmpfiles.org, temp.sh, x0.at, Gofile) are set up out of the box.
- Smart routing. Per-game destinations, size limits with fallbacks (a 40 MB clip goes to catbox and Discord gets the link), and destinations that receive every capture as well, such as a copy on a USB stick.
- Media gallery. Every capture with thumbnails, clips included, filtered by kind or by game (picked from the games you actually have captures of, named even when the game is a PS4 title or no longer installed), newest or oldest first. A check marks what has already been sent.
- Clip player. Full screen with sound, using FFmpeg (VP9, H.264, HEVC, AV1 with Opus or AAC), including the PS5's own recordings. Its buttons match [VLC for PS5](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC).
- Phone and PC. While PShare is open, any capture can be opened in a browser on the same network with the same controls, and the whole gallery can be browsed, streamed and downloaded. The setup page lets you paste webhooks and tokens from your phone instead of typing them with a controller.
- History with QR codes. Every upload, from the app or the background, with its link as a QR code to open on your phone. Failed ones can be retried

apps.name: VITA5
apps.summary: Plays a PS Vita on the PS5 over one USB cable.
apps.author: StonedModder

release.notes:
# Install

This app requires the official VitaUSBStream plugin from BMK-Studio: https://github.com/BMK-Studio/VitaUSBStream

No other USB streaming plugin is supported or will work.

Both devices must already run homebrew. The Vita needs VitaUSBStream. The PS5 needs a jailbreak with elfldr.

This release has three files.

## 1. Vita plugin

1. Copy `input_receiver.skprx` to `ur0:tai/` (VitaShell).
2. In `ur0:tai/config.txt`, under `*KERNEL`, put this line **above** `VitaUSBStream.skprx`:

```
*KERNEL
ur0:tai/input_receiver.skprx
ur0:tai/VitaUSBStream.skprx
```

3. Reboot the Vita. The input plugin must load before the stream plugin.

## 2. PS5 dock service

1. Make sure the PS5 payload loader is running.
2. Send `VITA5-payload.elf` to elfldr (port 9021).
3. Leave it running.

## 3. PS5 app

1. Extract `PPSA17035.zip`.
2. Copy the `PPSA17035` folder to `/data/homebrew/` over FTP (port 2120).
3. Every file and directory in that folder must be mode **0777**. If the app will not start, fix the modes first.
4. Close any older VITA5 title, then launch **PPSA17035** from the home screen.

Connect the Vita to the PS5 with one USB cable. The Vita's picture and sound play on the TV, and the DualSense controls the game.

apps.name: Surround Sound Studio
apps.summary: Plays surround test tones to check that audio passes through to your receiver.
apps.author: sainsaji

release.notes:
![](https://img.shields.io/badge/Release-v01.000.003-blueviolet?style=flat-square) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/PS5%20Hardware-Verified-0070d1?style=flat-square&logo=playstation&logoColor=white) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firmware-12.70-blue?style=flat-square)

**01.000.003:** the pauses of silence the app sends between format changes were four times too long on the TrueHD port, because its 768 kHz label is not the rate it really consumes frames at (192 kHz). They are now the intended length. The READMEs and the write-up also say plainly that Speaker Lab is EVO Player's Surround Sound Studio and that TrueHD works.

**01.000.002:** Dolby TrueHD now plays. It goes out as a MAT bitstream on a 768 kHz port, opened with the console's system audio calls (`sceAudioOutSysOpen` and `sceAudioOutSysConfigureOutput`), the route Sony's Blu-ray player uses. Hardware-tested on a PS5 Pro, firmware 12.70: it plays and the receiver shows "Dolby Audio".

**01.000.001:** a new icon, DTS-HD sent in the right console mode (it was going out as Atmos), AAC bursts that are valid for every frame length, and a settle time between format changes.

First release of **Surround Sound Studio**, a PS5 homebrew app for home-theatre sound. Please report problems.

**Passthrough page.** Plays test clips untouched over HDMI, so your soundbar or receiver decodes them:

- Dolby Digital, Dolby Digital Plus (including Atmos), DTS, AAC, Dolby TrueHD, DTS-HD, and Linear PCM (2ch and 6ch surround). TrueHD goes out as MAT through the console's system audio calls, the same route Sony's Blu-ray player uses; the receiver shows "Dolby Audio".
- Shows the formats your TV or receiver says it can decode, and every return code from the console.
- The bundled clips are channel-ID tones: each speaker beeps in turn, so a wrong channel map is easy to hear.
- Displays an "ATMOS" badge for Dolby Atmos clips (`local-atmos.eac3`).

**Speaker Lab page** (new, not yet tested on hardware). EVO Player's speaker test suite:

- A test tone on each speaker, and automatic 5.1 and 7.1 sequences.
- A 360 degree sweep, and a 3D sound field you can fly around the room.
- Calibration through the DualSense microphone: the level, distance and delay of each speaker, as a report.

Switch pages with **L1 / R1**; the tabs at the top show where you are.

**Install:** copy `PPSA99051.ffpfsc` to `/data/homebrew/` and start it with ShadowMount+, or unpack `PPSA99051.zip` into `/data/homebrew/`. Close the app before replacing it.

**Known limits:** While a bitstream plays, the console mutes the app's other sounds. After many format changes in a row the receiver can get stuck on its last format (a PCM clip labelled AAC, AAC silent); restarting the receiver clears it.
